title: Is This a Mandatory DV Arrest?

rel.q: Is there a domestic violence relationship?
rel.help: Current or former spouse or household member, child in common or expected, or dating relationship.

pc.q: Is there probable cause that a DV offense (predicate act) was committed?
pc.help: Assault, harassment, threats, criminal mischief, contempt, stalking and the other offenses listed in 2C:25-19.

injury.q: Does the victim show signs of injury caused by the DV?
injury.help: Read broadly: includes complaints of pain or impairment, not just visible marks.

warrant.q: Is there a warrant in effect for the suspect?

order.q: Is there probable cause a served restraining order was violated?

points: Arrest the suspect and sign a criminal complaint.
Seize weapons at risk, plus FPIC and permits with any firearm.
Give the victim notice of rights and complete the DV report.
You may arrest and/or sign a complaint based on probable cause.
Still seize weapons when needed and complete the DV report.

nopc.result: No probable cause for a DV offense
points: Complete the DV offense report anyway.
Give the victim notice of rights, including the right to seek a TRO.

notdv.result: Not covered by the DV Act
points: Handle any offense under regular criminal law.
Document the relationship facts in your report.
